economic_context_for_article.narrative: Sweden operates with modest fiscal space in 2026. IMF WEO April 2026 projects Swedish real GDP growth at approximately 1.7% for 2026, following recovery from the 2023–2024 slowdown. Government debt remains low by EU standards. The SfU21 welfare restriction is motivated primarily by migration policy rather than fiscal emergency — savings are estimated at SEK 1–2 billion annually, modest relative to total socialförsäkring spending of ~SEK 600+ billion. The SfU24 housing allowance reform may yield smaller but positive fiscal accuracy improvements.
